newsitem.title: USA: N.J. says may need Expressway toll hike -- paper.
newsitem.headline: N.J. says may need Expressway toll hike -- paper.

text.p: South Jersey Transportation Authority officials said they could not rule out the possibility of toll increases to cover the cost of a $330 million tunnel and roadway project, the Philadelphia Inquirer reported Thursday.
About $60 million of the project, part of a deal between the state and casino developer Steve Wynn, will be financed by the authority.

An authority spokesman told the paper that agency officials expect increased traffic alone will pay for the bonds to be issued for the project. But he said the agency would not rule out a toll increase on the Atlantic City Expressway, the first since 1969, if those projections are not met. Tolls are currently 25 cents.
Forecasts predict increased traffic levels of 40 percent, or 48 million cars a year. Even if only half that figure materializes it would be enough to pay for the bonds, the agency said.
In addition to the authority's contribution, the state's Transportation Trust Fund is contributing $95 million to the project. The Casino Reinvestment and Development Authority is paying $65 million.
